items.title: Linear perspective demonstrated
items.claim: Filippo Brunelleschi is credited with demonstrating linear perspective. Around when did he stage his famous Baptistery experiment in Florence?
items.reveal_title: About 1420 in front of Florence's Baptistery
items.reveal:
Brunelleschi's experiment, recorded by his biographer Manetti, used a painted panel with a hole and a mirror to demonstrate single-vanishing-point perspective.

Leon Battista Alberti formalised the method in De pictura (1435).
items.why: A technical innovation can reshape an entire visual culture within a generation.

items.title: What happened to the original Fountain
items.claim: Marcel Duchamp submitted Fountain, a signed urinal, to the Society of Independent Artists in New York in 1917. What is true about the original object today?

options.text: It is in the Met's permanent collection
It was lost; existing versions are 1960s replicas authorised by Duchamp
It is on permanent display at MoMA
It was destroyed at the original exhibition

items.reveal_title: The original was lost; all 'Fountains' are later replicas
items.reveal:
The Society of Independent Artists never displayed it; the original disappeared. From the 1960s Duchamp authorised replicas, now in collections including the Tate and Centre Pompidou.

A 2004 survey of 500 art-world figures voted Fountain the most influential artwork of the 20th century.
items.why: Conceptual art's value can attach to the idea, not the original object.

items.title: The first Impressionist show
items.claim: What was the first Impressionist exhibition called?

options.text: Exposition of the Anonymous Society of Painters, Sculptors and Engravers

items.reveal:
The exhibition opened on 15 April 1874 in Nadar's former studio. The label 'Impressionists' came from a critic, Louis Leroy, mocking Monet's Impression, soleil levant.

The group held eight exhibitions between 1874 and 1886.
items.why: Movement names often come from hostile critics rather than the artists themselves.

items.title: The painting most cited as Cubism's origin
items.claim: Which 1907 Picasso painting is most often cited as a key precursor to Cubism?
items.reveal:
Picasso painted the work in 1907 but did not exhibit it publicly until 1916. The fractured planes and reference to Iberian and African sculpture set the conditions for Cubism with Braque.

It is now in MoMA, New York.
items.why: A painting can remain influential through private circulation among artists before reaching the public.

items.title: Kandinsky and abstraction
items.claim: Wassily Kandinsky's 1911 book Concerning the Spiritual in Art argued for non-representational painting drawing on what analogy?

options.text: Music as a purely formal art moving the soul

items.reveal:
Kandinsky argued colour and form could affect viewers directly, as harmony and rhythm do in music.

His Compositions and Improvisations are titled after musical genres.
items.why: Abstraction needed a theoretical framework before audiences could read it as art.

items.title: Warhol's first soup cans
items.claim: Andy Warhol's first Campbell's Soup Cans exhibition was in which city in 1962?
items.reveal:
The 32 canvases (one per Campbell's variety) were priced at around $100 each. Ferus's owner Irving Blum bought the entire series for around $1,000 and later sold it to MoMA for around $15 million.

The work consolidated Pop Art's place in American museums within a decade.
items.why: Pop Art's commercial trajectory mirrored the consumer culture it depicted.

items.title: Emin's My Bed
items.claim: Tracey Emin's My Bed was shortlisted for the Turner Prize in 1999. In 2014 it sold at auction. For approximately how much?
items.reveal:
Christie's London sold My Bed for around £2.5 million (with buyer's premium) on 1 July 2014.

The work was later loaned to the Tate by Count Christian Duerckheim.
items.why: Markets give surprising answers to questions about value in conceptual and autobiographical art.

items.title: Banksy's self-shredding
items.claim: In October 2018 a Banksy work partially shredded during a Sotheby's auction. What happened to the price after the stunt?

options.text: It sold for the auction price, then resold in 2021 for around £18.6 million
The buyer sued and won damages

items.reveal:
Originally hammered at around £1 million on 5 October 2018, the partially shredded work was renamed Love Is in the Bin and resold in October 2021 for around £18.6 million.

The shredder was concealed in the frame.
items.why: Critiques of art markets can become market assets themselves.

items.title: The most expensive painting sold
items.claim: Which painting holds the auction record set in November 2017?
items.reveal:
The Leonardo attribution to Salvator Mundi remains contested by some scholars. The buyer was reportedly acting for the Saudi crown prince.

The painting has not been publicly displayed since the sale.
items.why: Attribution debates and market records are intertwined in the history of major paintings.

items.title: Kahlo's body of work
items.claim: Roughly what proportion of Frida Kahlo's known paintings are self-portraits?
items.reveal_title: Roughly one third of around 150 works
items.reveal:
Standard catalogues list around 150 paintings, of which approximately 55 are self-portraits. Kahlo wrote that she painted herself 'because I am so often alone, because I am the subject I know best'.

Her first US museum retrospective opened only in 1978, 24 years after her death.
items.why: Recognition timing shapes how an artist's body of work is constructed by curators and historians.

items.title: AI image generation and copyright
items.claim: The US Copyright Office issued guidance in 2023 about generative-AI images. What did it say about purely AI-generated outputs?

options.text: They are fully copyrightable by the prompter
Purely machine-generated content without human authorship is not copyrightable in the US
All such images are public domain worldwide

items.reveal_title: Human authorship is required for US copyright
items.reveal:
The US Copyright Office's March 2023 statement and subsequent rulings (e.g. Zarya of the Dawn) required identifiable human authorial contribution.

The Andersen v. Stability AI and related cases continue to test the boundaries.
items.why: Legal frameworks for what counts as an authored work are being negotiated in real time.

items.title: How long Banksy has remained anonymous
items.claim: Banksy first appeared as a graffiti artist in Bristol in the early 1990s. Roughly how long has the identity remained publicly unconfirmed?
items.reveal_title: Around three decades of unconfirmed identity
items.reveal:
Despite litigation that has compelled disclosures in specific contexts, no public identification has been confirmed by the artist.

Anonymity itself is treated by some critics as part of the work's conceptual structure.
items.why: Identity can be a deliberately deployed element of an artistic practice.
